articles.title: Bam Adebayo feels like the 'scapegoat' amid struggles, Heat's 0-4 start to the season
articles.summary: The Dallas Mavericks beat Miami 113-109 on Monday night despite a triple-double from new Heat star Giannis Antetokounmpo.
articles.body:
Bam Adebayo is not OK with taking the blame for the Miami Heat's brutal 0-4 start to the season.

The Heat star, after the team fell 113-109 to the Dallas Mavericks on Monday night, said he feels singled out for the franchise's struggles — especially after it landed Giannis Antetokounmpo in a blockbuster deal this past offseason.

"You know, it's funny how the outside noise wants to make me the scapegoat," Adebayo said, via ESPN . "But when the tables turn, just all that energy, when the energy shifts, just be prepared for that."

Though it's not fair to put all of the blame on Adebayo, he has struggled in the early stretch of the season. Adebayo is averaging just 11.8 points and 7.3 rebounds per game, and is only shooting 16.7% from the 3-point line. He had just eight points and went 3-of-10 on Monday night, and missed all five of his attempts from behind the arc.

Antetokounmpo, meanwhile, had a triple-double with 29 points, 14 rebounds and 11 assists.

By comparison, Adebayo averaged 20.1 points and 10 rebounds per game last season. He even dropped 83 points in a single game in March, which is the second-most scored by a player in a single contest in NBA history. Only Wilt Chamberlain's 100-point game in 1962 sits ahead of him on that list.

For now, Adebayo said his struggles are simply because his shot is not going in. It's nothing more.

"I got expectations for myself, but, obviously, the outside noise got expectations for us," he said. "So for me, I know what I'm capable of. I'm not going to overthink that. We're 0-4 right now. I'd rather it be right now than this be midway through the season or in April. Because what if we go on a 10-game winning streak? Then how does the noise change?"

The Heat will take on the Atlanta Hawks next on Wednesday. A loss there would match their worst start since the 2007-08 campaign. The Heat also currently hold the worst record in the league, though four other franchises are also still searching for their first wins.

Miami still has time to figure out how all the pieces work together now that Antetokounmpo is in the mix. Bam's numbers falling from last season seemed inevitable after the trade. But so far, it's not been a good start.

"It's not just Bam, it's everybody," Antetokounmpo said. "You know, everybody — we try to figure out where we fit in and what we gotta do. Kind of try to not step on our toes."

articles.title: Jalen Brunson, Knicks surge past Pistons to end losing streak after NBA Finals win
articles.summary: The Knicks were the first defending champion in 15 years to drop their first three games of the season.
articles.body:
New York Knicks fans can finally relax. The defending champions, at long last, have won a game.

After dropping three straight to start the season , the Knicks flew ahead in the second half to beat the Detroit Pistons 111-97 on Tuesday night at Madison Square Garden. Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns combined for 50 points in the win, and helped power a huge third quarter that allowed the Knicks to roll to the win without much issue down the stretch.

The Knicks had looked, well, a step slow to start the new season. They fell to LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers in their season opener, then dropped single-digit games to both the Boston Celtics and Orlando Magic over the next several days.

That made them the first defending champions since the Dallas Mavericks in 2011-12 to open the next season with three straight losses. While that was a shortened season after an NBA lockout, the Mavericks ended up going 36-30 that campaign and were eliminated in the first round of the playoffs.

It looked early as if the Pistons were going to roll to the win in Manhattan. They were in control for much of the first half, and even took a 13-point lead briefly in the second quarter. But the Knicks mounted an 18-3 run to tie the game and eventually take a one-point advantage into the locker room. Brunson scored 11 points in the first 24 minutes, but went only 1-of-9 from the field. Cade Cunningham, meanwhile, was well on his way to a triple-double with 15 points, 7 rebounds and 6 assists.

Brunson shook off that poor offensive start almost immediately in the third quarter. He drilled a layup and then an easy 20-footer over Cunningham to help power an 11-0 burst out of the break and force a quick Detroit timeout. That gave the Knicks their first double-digit lead of the night.

Things quickly spiraled from there for the Pistons. New York ended up outscoring Detroit 37-13 in the period to take a 25-point lead into the fourth quarter. The Pistons shot just 4 of 19 from the field in the third quarter.

Detroit wasn't coming back from that. The Knicks cruised the rest of the way, and fended off one final push in the fourth quarter, to take the 14-point win. The Pistons never got within single digits again.

Towns led the Knicks with 27 points and 20 rebounds in the win. Brunson added 23 points and seven assists, despite shooting just 5 of 18 from the field. Landry Shamet and OG Anunoby each put up 13 points.

Paul Reed led the Pistons with 22 points and nine rebounds, and Cunningham finished with 19 points, 9 rebounds and 8 assists. The Pistons were undefeated entering Tuesday's contest, and now sit at 3-1 on the year.

The Knicks have a long way to go to actually defend their championship. No team has pulled that off since the Golden State Warriors nearly a decade ago.

But the Knicks now have a win on the books this fall. That's the first step.

articles.title: Stephen Curry celebrates wife Ayesha’s career first as her latest move takes her beyond the kitchen and into holiday movies
articles.summary: Ayesha Curry has her first leading role in a feature film, and her husband was quick to react.
articles.body: Ayesha Curry has her first leading role in a feature film, and her husband was quick to react. Roku released the trailer and premiere date for “Second Chance Holiday” on Tuesday, October 27, almost four months after naming her the headliner in July. Stephen Curry posted his response on Instagram once the news was out. The holiday romantic comedy casts her as a dating expert opposite Matthew Daddario. It starts streaming on the Roku Channel on November 5.Stephen Curry backs Ayesha Curry’s first leading film roleStephen Curry marked the moment on Instagram Stories with a short greeting for Ayesha: “My Leading Lady.” He wrote that he sees the work behind the scenes, and that the public now gets to watch her shine. The Golden State Warriors star added that this is only the beginning.Ayesha plays Chelsey Banks, a dating expert who keeps getting dumped around the holidays. She goes home for a fresh start and runs into her high school sweetheart, played by Daddario. Roku describes her streak as a possible curse, or maybe the universe nudging her back to her first love.Maxwell McGuire directs from a script by Erin Muroski. Muse Entertainment produced the film with Motion Entertainment. Dennis Andres and Arlene Duncan co-star, and viewers can stream it free.Ayesha said in a July statement she “fell in love with” Chelsey while bringing her to life.Ayesha Curry’s acting credits before the lead roleActing is not new to her. Ayesha landed small parts as a child actor on Hannah Montana and Good Luck Charlie, then turned up later in Ballers and A Black Lady Sketch Show. Netflix’s Irish Wish put her opposite Lindsay Lohan in 2024. Last year she played a TV host in Hulu’s Joy to the World, a supporting turn in another holiday comedy.The top billing is what changes this time. Until now, she had never carried a feature film.GOAT, an animated film, premiered in February. Curry produced it and appeared in it, while Ayesha voiced Carol, the manager of Whiskers Diner.The couple also share a Broadway credit. articles.title: Pedro Martínez advierte a su Real Madrid tras nueve victorias seguidas
articles.standfirst: "No podemos pensar que vamos a ganar todos los partidos"
articles.summary: "No podemos pensar que vamos a ganar todos los partidos"
articles.body: El entrenador del Real Madrid, Pedro Martínez, avisó tras ganar a Kosner Baskonia que no pueden pensar que van a ganar todos los partidos porque ahora estén en una dinámica ganadora (suman nueve victorias consecutivas tras perder 102-98 ante el Hapoel en Euroliga el 1 de octubre). El técnico adelantó en sala de prensa que van a perder partidos, "no podemos pensar que vamos a ganar todos los partidos", pero espera que sea "lo más extraordinario posible". Valoró que fue "un buen partido" y destacó que jugaron bien en ataque, "compartiendo bien el balón y leyendo la defensa". Reconoció que tuvieron más problemas en defensa por la dificultad que supone frenar a los azulgranas. "Tienen buen uno contra uno y un rápido primer paso", añadió. Sin embargo, el entrenador del equipo blanco matizó su victoria por las condiciones del rival. "Han luchado hasta el final, su situación no es de buena con tres jugadores muy importantes lesionados", consideró y explicó que les ha favorecido. "Con otro Baskonia las dificultades serán mucho mayores", agregó el entrenador, que puso en valor la mentalidad de su equipo. "Es muy importante mantenernos en una línea y estar todos en la misma página. No nos creemos superiores a nadie y creemos que tenemos mucho margen de mejora", señaló Pedro Madrid, que sabe que a algunos jugadores les está costando entrar en dinámica. "Es muy importante crecer cuando lleguen los momentos competitivos, pero todos los momentos son muy importantes", deslizó.

articles.title: Jayson Tatum lifts Celtics past Nets with OT buzzer-beater after brutal Mikel Brown blunder
articles.summary: Mikel Brown tried to force a layup and missed at the other end instead of taking a foul, which set up Jayson Tatum's game winner on Tuesday night in Boston.
articles.body:
Jayson Tatum called game on Tuesday night, but only after a brutal mistake from Mikel Brown on the other end.

Tatum drilled a buzzer-beater to lift the Boston Celtics past the Brooklyn Nets 125-124 on Tuesday. He took two dribbles off an inbounds pass and expertly pulled up from the elbow to hit a jumper he's made countless times in his career right as time expired.

Tatum simply jogged the other way with his hand in the air as TD Garden erupted.

That shot was only made possible after Brown made a critical mistake on the other end. With the Nets up by one, all Brown had to do was sit tight and take a foul or let time expire. There were only seconds remaining on the clock, and absolutely no need to rush things.

Instead, Brown saw a path to the rim and took it. He missed the left-handed layup and crashed down to the court hard as the Celtics took possession.

That gave Boston one final chance, which Tatum capitalized on.

"It's a broken play. I blame me," Brown said, via the New York Post's Brian Lewis . "We weren't supposed to switch that and I switched it. Made a couple of mistakes down the stretch that hurt us. "So I'm gonna take the blame on it, learn from it [and] get prepared for next game."

"It's a broken play. I blame me," Brown said, via the New York Post's Brian Lewis . "We weren't supposed to switch that and I switched it. Made a couple of mistakes down the stretch that hurt us.

"So I'm gonna take the blame on it, learn from it [and] get prepared for next game."

Tatum finished with 40 points and eight assists, and made a career-high 18 free throws in the win for the Celtics. Paul George had 20 points with 7 rebounds and 7 assists, and Derrick White finished with 16 points. The win was Boston's third in a row, and the Celtics now sit at 3-1 on the new season.

Brown's mistake is going to overshadow everything else, and rightfully so, but he had an impressive night otherwise. Brown, who the Nets took with the No. 6 overall draft pick out of Louisville earlier this year, had 17 points off the bench and hit an off-balanced 3-pointer to send the game into overtime.

The Nets were in lockstep with the Celtics nearly the entire way. White put the Celtics up by five with just 13 seconds left in regulation with a pair of free throws. But Brown scored five straight points himself, including two more at the stripe after a take foul, to keep the Nets alive.

Michael Porter Jr. led the Nets with 27 points and 12 rebounds, and Julius Randle added 24 points and nine rebounds. The loss dropped the Nets to 0-4 on the season.

While the rookie mistake is going to linger, Brown appears to be off to a solid start in his NBA career. Leaving Tatum with time to spare in a critical moment of a game likely isn't something he's going to do again.

articles.title: Lawyers for RJ Luis Jr. Ask Judge to Block SEC From Intervening to Keep Him Off LSU's Roster
articles.summary: Lawyers for RJ Luis Jr., who was briefly under contract with two NBA teams in 2025 but never played in a game, are asking a Louisiana judge to block the Southeastern Conference from punishing LSU if Luis is added to the Tigers' roster.
articles.body:
Lawyers for RJ Luis Jr., who was briefly under contract with two NBA teams in 2025 but never played in a game, are asking a Louisiana judge to block the Southeastern Conference from punishing LSU if Luis is added to the Tigers' roster.

The request was included in a petition filed Tuesday in state district court in East Baton Rouge Parish, where Judge Ronald R. Johnson in late August granted a preliminary injunction against the NCAA, which has argued that Luis is ineligible to play.

An SEC spokesman said Tuesday that the conference had no immediate comment on the new filing. The SEC already has accused LSU in a related federal case of exhibiting an "ongoing defiance of the conference's professionalism rules" by trying to add Luis to its roster.

The SEC has a long-established rule forbidding teams from adding players with major professional experience to their rosters. In September, the conference announced updated enforcement provisions to that rule, stating that the commissioner had the power to suspend coaches, fine universities up to half of a sport's budget and restrict a member university's voting privileges on conference matters.

Under threat of being voted out of the SEC by fellow league members, LSU elected in early September not to add to its football roster two players who'd spent part of the offseason with NFL clubs before being recruited back to college by Tigers first-year coach Lane Kiffin.

Those players — Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris — had played for Kiffin at Mississippi. During Week 1 of the season, they were granted a preliminary injunction against the NCAA and SEC by another state judge in Baton Rouge.

That case led the SEC to file a federal case alleging that LSU, by attempting to circumvent SEC rules, was violating the league's First Amendment right to freedom of association. In other words, the SEC essentially argued it has the right to enforce rules governing competition among members who all chose to join the league.

Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill has mocked the SEC for taking that position, calling its federal case "garbage." She has filed briefs supporting LSU and urging dismissal of the case, in which she has since been named as a defendant.

The attorneys who filed Thursday's petition in state court in Louisiana — Elliot Abrams of Raleigh, North Carolina, and Tony Clayton of Baton Rouge — represent only Luis. They do not represent LSU, and have asked the judge to also block LSU from following any SEC directives that would bar Luis from playing.

"LSU has not rostered Mr. Luis, and the reason it has given is the Conference's protocols," Luis' petition states. "This court enjoined the NCAA, and everyone acting in concert or participation with it, from keeping RJ Luis Jr. off the floor at LSU this season, directly or indirectly. The Southeastern Conference's policy is what keeps him off the floor now."

Luis, the 2025 Big East Player of the Year with St. John's, played three seasons of college basketball with two teams before declaring for the 2025 NBA draft.

He went undrafted, but briefly was under contract with Utah and Boston. Will Wade, hired last spring to coach LSU for the second time, recruited Luis to return to college.

The NCAA balked at allowing Luis to regain his eligibility because he'd elected to leave college for the NBA and never followed NCAA protocols for retaining eligibility by withdrawing from the NBA draft.

articles.title: Warriors’ Stephen Curry sends heartwarming 7-word message to Charlotte Hornets legend’s news
articles.summary: The Charlotte Hornets announced Tuesday that they will retire Muggsy Bogues’ No. 1 jersey, and Stephen Curry sent his congratulations in just seven words.
articles.body: The Charlotte Hornets announced Tuesday that they will retire Muggsy Bogues’ No. 1 jersey, and Stephen Curry sent his congratulations in just seven words. The Warriors superstar grew up in Charlotte while father Dell Curry played for the Hornets, so the news hit close to home. The ceremony is set for halftime of the Hornets’ game against the Milwaukee Bucks on Feb. 11, 2027, at Spectrum Center. Bogues found out while filming what he thought was a Jr. NBA promo, when the script on the screen said otherwise.What did Stephen Curry say about Muggsy Bogues’ jersey retirement?Stephen Curry wrote, “Yessir there’s only one Muggy Bogues. Congratulations.” He was among the people who reached out after the Hornets shared the reveal video on Instagram.The link goes back decades. Dell Curry played in Charlotte from 1987 to 1998, which put his son in the same locker rooms as Bogues, the Hornets’ primary playmaker in the 1990s. Dell’s No. 30 is already retired there. Bobby Phills’ No. 13 is the other. Bogues will be the third.The reveal was a setup. Bogues sat down to read a teleprompter for what he believed was a Jr. NBA and Jr. WNBA video, and the lines turned out to announce his own night. He got emotional as Dell Curry and Hornets staff told him how much he deserved it. Bogues said he can’t wait to share the night with his family and the fans.Why are the Hornets retiring Muggsy Bogues’ No. 1 jersey?Bogues is the shortest player in NBA history at 5-foot-3. The average player during his career stood 6-foot-7 and weighed 213 pounds, which made him 16 inches shorter and 77 pounds lighter. Before the league, he helped Dunbar High School in Baltimore go 60-0 across his junior and senior seasons.Washington drafted him 12th in 1987, and Charlotte took him in the 1988 expansion draft. He stayed through 1998 and is still the franchise leader in assists, steals and minutes. In 632 games with the Hornets, he averaged 8.8 points and 8.8 assists.Over 14 NBA seasons he averaged 7.7 points and 7.6 assists, and only eight players from the 1987 draft class played more games. He was also part of the franchise’s first playoff series win in 1993.Bogues said when the jersey goes up, “it’ll be like I’m the one looking down at the entire world.” Co-chairmen Rick Schnall and Gabe Plotkin called him “a role model for generations.”He has been a Hornets ambassador since 2014.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Tatum desata la locura en Boston: 40 puntos y tiro ganador sobre la bocina de la prórroga
articles.standfirst: El alero acaba con la resistencia de los Nets con la séptima canasta al límite que anota en su carrera
articles.summary: El alero acaba con la resistencia de los Nets con la séptima canasta al límite que anota en su carrera
articles.body: Una canasta de Jayson Tatum sobre la bocina de la prórroga coronó su gran noche y dio el triunfo a los Celtics (125-124). El alero anotó 40 puntos (10/20 en tiros de campo y 18/22 desde el tiro libre) para acabar con la resistencia de los Nets dirigidos por Jordi Fernández. Los de Brooklyn, que aún no conocen la victoria después de cuatro partidos, llevaron al límite a su rival, forzaron el tiempo extra y sólo cedieron ante la genialidad de una de la grandes estrellas de la NBA. Una vez más, Tatum le ganó al tiempo. Es la séptima vez que en su carrera que anota un tiro ganador con menos de tres segundos por jugar en el cronómetro. Desde la temporada 2019-20, nadie ha dado más triunfos al límite a su equipo. Los Celtics suman su tercera victoria seguida y sólo perdieron en el debut ante los Pistons, cuando desperdiciaron 22 puntos de ventaja. Esta vez restaban 2,3 cuando Derrick White puso el balón en juego en un saque de banda, encontró al alero en la línea del triple, se dio la vuelta rápidamente y en ese movimiento ya sacó ventaja a los dos defensores que le acosaban, Mike Brown Jr. y Keon Ellis. Se colocó frente al aro y lanzó desde cinco metros. El balón entró casi limpio y se desató la locura en la grada del TD Garden y sobre la cancha. Hugo González apenas pudo aportar en los seis minutos que disputó. Se quedó sin anotar tras fallar un tiro de dos y un triple y atrapó dos rebotes. Venía de sumar sus primeros puntos de la temporada (13 a los Bulls) y disputar 24 minutos, pero se ha quedado a cero en tres de los cuatro partidos disputados. Al tiempo extra se llegó después de un desenlace en el que los Celtics no supieron cerrar el partido. Ganaban por 116-111 a falta de 13 segundos después de que White anotara desde la personal. Brown hizo lo suyo para los Nets. Tatum se dejó un tiro libre cuando restaban cuatro segundos, aunque el partido parecía decantado: 117-113. Julius Randle, también. Los visitantes le hicieron falta a Mitchell Robinson, que falló sus dos lanzamientos desde el 4,60. En la última acción, Brown anotó un triple con dos décimas por jugar para forzar la prórroga. Ahí, los Nets mandaban por 119-124 a falta de dos minutos. No volvieron a anotar. Tatum y Paul George, que acabó con 20 puntos, acercaron a Boston con sendos tiros libres. El novato Brown, que anotó 17 puntos, pasó de ser el héroe por ese tiro que forzó el tiempo extra a fallar una bandeja cuando restaban sólo 2,3 segundos para la conclusión. Eso fue lo que permitió a Tatum resolver el choque. Michael Porter Jr., con 27+12, y Julius Randle, con 24 puntos, fueron los mejores de los Nets.

articles.title: Malik Beasley acuerda declararse culpable por amaño de apuestas en la NBA
articles.standfirst: Se le acusa de manipular su rendimiento en cuatro partidos de la temporada 2023-24, cuando militaba en los Bucks
articles.summary: Se le acusa de manipular su rendimiento en cuatro partidos de la temporada 2023-24, cuando militaba en los Bucks
articles.body: Malik Beasley, imputado por la Fiscalía de Estados Unidos en un caso de amaño de apuestas deportivas ilegales, ha acordado declararse culpable, según informó este martes su defensa. Beasley, que jugó nueve temporadas en la NBA entre 2016 y 2025, se declarará culpable el próximo 9 de diciembre en un tribunal de Nueva York, según detalló The Athletic, citando al abogado del deportista, Steve Haney. Beasley llevaba tiempo negociando con los fiscales encargados de la investigación, que en junio pasado imputaron cargos contra él y contra el también exjugador de la NBA Ed Davis. Beasley y Davis, que compartieron vestuario en la temporada 2020-21 en los Minnesota Timberwolves, se sumaron a Terry Rozier, Jontay Porter y Damon Jones, implicados en casos parecidos anteriores. Según la acusación, Davis y Beasley se pusieron de acuerdo para manipular el rendimiento de este último en cuatro partidos de la temporada 2023-24. En ese momento Davis militaba en los Cleveland Cavaliers y Beasley en los Milwaukee Bucks. A pesar de haber ganado más de 60 millones de dólares a lo largo de su carrera, Beasley acumuló millones de dólares en deudas de juego, por lo que Davis le prestó dinero. Según la acusación, el jugador habría saldado parte de esa deuda con Davis participando en el presunto amaño de apuestas relacionadas, entre otros parámetros, con su número de rebotes. "La única forma de ganarle a Las Vegas (las casas de apuestas) es apostando en deportes. En todo lo demás, tienen ventaja", escribió Davis a Beasley en un mensaje de texto incluido en la acusación. El plan se habría venido abajo cuando Beasley no logró quedar por debajo de la cifra de rebotes fijada para las apuestas en el último de los cuatro partidos investigados, contra los Brooklyn Nets. La Fiscalía imputó a otras tres personas en el caso, incluyendo el agente de Davis, todos con varios cargos en su contra. Beasley disputó con los Detroit Pistons su última temporada en la NBA en la 2024-25 y negociaba una renovación por tres años y 42 millones de dólares cuando la franquicia retiró la oferta tras ser informada de que el jugador estaba siendo investigado. En total, Beasley disputó nueve temporadas en la NBA, mientras que Davis permaneció doce años en activo.

articles.title: Damian Lillard powers Trail Blazers past Luka Dončić, Lakers to remain undefeated
articles.summary: The Lakers' undefeated run to start the season has finally come to an end.
articles.body:
Luka Dončić did everything he could to try and power the Los Angeles Lakers to a fourth straight win on Tuesday night. It just wasn't enough to get past Damian Lillard and Ja Morant.

The Portland Trail Blazers, thanks to a huge bucket from Morant late and a huge step-back 3-pointer from Lillard in the final minute, fended off Dončić and the Lakers to grab a 136-129 win on Tuesday at Crypto.com Arena. That pushed Portland to 3-0, its best start since 2022, and ended LA's three-game win streak to start the 2026-27 campaign.

While the contest was tight throughout, it wasn't until vintage Lillard showed up that the Blazers were able to seal the deal. Lillard, after faking to get Matisse Thybulle in the air in the corner, expertly stepped back to hit his bucket on the wing. That was the 36-year-old's fourth 3-pointer of the night.

That was enough to put the Lakers away, and push the Blazers to the seven-point win.

Dončić certainly tried to power the Lakers to the win Tuesday, which came just days after a 52-point performance against the Utah Jazz. Dončić scored a game-high 41 points and had nine assists against the Trail Blazers. He went 6-of-15 from behind the arc, including a ridiculously-deep triple down the stretch that kept the game close.

Austin Reaves added 26 points and seven assists for the Lakers, and Sandro Mamukelashvili finished with 17 off the bench. A win for the Lakers on Tuesday night would have matched the best start in team history since the 2010-11 campaign, which was led by Hall of Famer Kobe Bryant.

Lillard is in his first season back on the floor this fall. He missed all of last season recovering from an Achilles injury he suffered with the Milwaukee Bucks the season prior, and then he signed a three-year deal to rejoin the franchise where he got his start in 2025.

Lillard ended the night with 21 points and five rebounds. Morant, also in his first season with the Trail Blazers after his blockbuster trade out of Memphis, led the team with 23 points after shooting 9-of-13 from the field. Deni Avdija had 23 points and nine assists, and Jrue Holiday added 22 points off the bench. Portland, despite the win, missed 15 free throws.

While it's still very early, the Morant-Lillard pairing is clearly off to a great start up in Portland.

articles.title: New York Knicks 111-97 Detroit Pistons: Reigning champions Knicks beat Pistons for first win of the season
articles.summary: Reigning champions the New York Knicks had lost their first three games of the new season but rallied to beat the Detroit Pistons 111-97; Coach Mike Brown said: "We're more than capable if we put our minds to it, and that's what we've got to continue to try to build off"
articles.body:
Down by 13 points after one quarter, they outscored the Pistons 63-25 across the next two, putting the kind of numbers on the scoreboard they did repeatedly during their march to the NBA championship.

They beat the previously undefeated Pistons 111-97 on Tuesday night for their first victory after starting the season with three straight losses.

"We had more good moments in this game in totality than we did the first three games and that's why we got the win," coach Mike Brown said.

The Knicks opened the season with as many losses in three games as they had in 19 games during the playoffs. They went 16-3 and set a record for the largest point differential by a team in a postseason.

They returned this season with losses to Philadelphia, Boston and Orlando, and with another loss Tuesday would have joined the 1969-70 Celtics as the only reigning champions to lose their first four games.

That came after Hall of Fame center Bill Russell retired after the Celtics' run of 11 titles in 13 years. These Knicks have their entire starting five back, led by NBA Finals MVP Jalen Brunson and fellow All-Star Karl-Anthony Towns, but hadn't been delivering.

The Pistons, who handled the Knicks easily in all three regular-season meetings in 2025-26, jumped out to a 38-25 lead before New York limited them to 12 points in the second quarter.

"I thought we did a great job, like I said, picking up the physicality, a lot of energy in the game, looking more like ourselves from last year," Towns said.

"But we still have a lot of growing to do and tomorrow's another day for us to test ourselves and get better."

Towns finished with 27 points and 20 rebounds, but the Knicks didn't truly find their rhythm until Brunson began to break out of his early-season slump. He made his first three shots in the third quarter to start an 11-0 run that turned a one-point halftime lead into a 62-50 advantage.

"I was just trying to do things to help my team and things will turn eventually," Brunson said.

Brown cautioned that the Knicks will have hiccups throughout the long season as they aim to peak in the playoffs as they did last season.

"So is it fixed? No, it ain't fixed. Nothing's really fixed," Brown said. "What tonight shows us is we're more than capable if we put our minds to it, and that's what we've got to continue to try to build off."

articles.title: China says takes Mbappe apology 'seriously' after Mao remark
articles.summary: China said Wednesday it took "seriously" an apology from Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe after comments he made poking fun at Mao Zedong sparked a social...
articles.body:
China said Wednesday it took "seriously" an apology from Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe after comments he made poking fun at Mao Zedong sparked a social media storm and saw Spanish football yanked off state TV.

Mocking former leader Mao -- blamed by historians for millions of deaths -- is taboo in China and the French player's remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure to anger Beijing.

The clip of the video interview with French show The Bridge -- since taken down -- saw Mbappe talk about being amused by an internet meme of his face photoshopped onto "some guy, think he's a Chinese dictator", an apparent reference to Mao.

"My comment was ill-judged and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset," the France captain said in a statement in French, Chinese and English on Tuesday.

Foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing on Wednesday: "We take seriously the apology the individual concerned has made."

But that may not be the end of the matter.

La Liga, which has seen the broadcast of its matches suspended in China, said it "deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe's recent comments have caused among Chinese fans".

Chinese beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year's World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe, said Tuesday it had scrapped its partnership with the player, as did dairy firms Mengniu and Milkground.

CMG, which oversees public broadcaster CCTV, said it had decided to suspend broadcasts of the world's second-richest football league after England's Premier League.

The 27-year-old continued to face a torrent of criticism from Chinese web users on Wednesday, some of it racist.

"His remarks were hurtful toward China and the Chinese people, so they cannot be translated," wrote one user on social media platform Weibo.

Mbappe's original joke about Mao was not reposted -- or had been scrubbed -- from China's tightly controlled social media.

Chinese social media app Xiaohongshu had meanwhile frozen Mbappe's account, where he has over a million followers.

The same was done on the Weibo app, with a notice stating that "the user has been banned from following due to violating laws or the Weibo Community Convention".

Some Chinese media reports said global brands like Dior and Hublot had removed their Mbappe-related content on Weibo.

An AFP search on Dior and Hublot's Weibo page with Mbappe's Chinese name produced no results.

Offline too the Mbappe brand appeared to be under threat.

When AFP visited the Adidas flagship store in Beijing's Sanlitun shopping district, Real Madrid shirts were available for sale, but none bearing the striker's name.

Mbappe merchandise including unofficial jerseys, beanies and caps remain available on retail app Taobao.

Chinese state media have previously praised Mbappe as a "footballing sensation" and "talent", with the forward well-loved by fans in the country.

His face is plastered on billboards, on soft drinks and across social media.

Mbappe is also sometimes affectionately referred to as "Guigui", meaning "turtle" in Chinese, for his resemblance to a character from the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles movie.

Other major overseas sports leagues have previously angered China.

China suspended sponsorship deals with the NBA while the state broadcaster pulled NBA games off Chinese television for a year in October 2019.

This followed Houston Rockets executive Daryl Morey tweeting "Fight for freedom, stand with Hong Kong", referring to protests Beijing called separatist and seditious.

"In this era of economic globalisation, an increasing number of celebrities are stepping onto the global stage, engaging with fans and business partners from diverse cultural backgrounds," the official People's Daily said in an opinion piece this week.

"Learning how to respect different nations and cultures is an essential lesson.

"Respecting the history, culture, social customs and national sentiments of others is a fundamental principle for cross-border interaction, a standard of conduct widely upheld by the international community."

articles.title: Machacón Wembanyama: nueve mates, tope de su carrera
articles.standfirst: El pívot de los Spurs rompe a los Kings con 29 puntos, 10 rebotes y cinco tapones
articles.summary: El pívot de los Spurs rompe a los Kings con 29 puntos, 10 rebotes y cinco tapones
articles.body: Hasta nueve veces se colgó del aro Victor Wembanyama en el cómodo triunfo de los Spurs sobre los débiles Kings, que todavía no conocen la victoria (130-103). El pívot francés abusó de su rival igualando su récord de mates en la NBA. Acabó con 29 puntos, 10 rebotes y cinco tapones. Dominio absoluto de los tableros pese al 20+14 de Domantas Sabonis, que tuvo mucho menos peso en el partido. Si es que se le puede llamar así a lo visto en el Frost Bank Center de San Antonio. Porque el control de los Spurs fue absoluto. El primer cuarto sirvió de calentamiento: 39-29. Para entonces, Wembanyama ya sumaba 15 puntos con 7/10 en tiros de campo y cuatro de ellos habían sido mates. Al descanso, los locales ya habían metido 80 puntos y ganaban por 26. No es una desventaja insalvable en estos tiempos, pero sí para los Kings, lejos aún de ser un equipo. En la primera victoria en casa de los aspirantes Spurs brilló también Julian Champagnie. Saliendo del banquillo, se fue a los 26 puntos demostrando de nuevo que ha empezado el curso con la mirilla ajustada: 8/13 en triples. Dylan Harper llegó a los 13 puntos y añadió seis rebotes y seis asistencias. Todos los titulares de San Antonio alcanzaron la decena de puntos en un triunfo coral ante una defensa lastimosa, la tercera peor en este inicio de campeonato. Junto a Sabonis, los más destacado en los Kings fueron De'Andre Hunter, con 24 puntos, y Zach LaVine, con 22. El novato Darius Acuff Jr. llegó otra vez a los 20 lanzamientos de campo, récord en la historia de la NBA para los cuatro primeros partidos de una carrera. Metió 19 puntos.

articles.title: Crisis total en el Baskonia: insólita pitada al presidente Querejeta
articles.standfirst: El dirigente fue abucheado durante el partido ante el Real Madrid por un Buesa Arena medio vacío que le recriminó las últimas decisiones del club
articles.summary: El dirigente fue abucheado durante el partido ante el Real Madrid por un Buesa Arena medio vacío que le recriminó las últimas decisiones del club
articles.body: La crisis en el Kosner Baskonia ya es a todos los niveles. No sólo está en la cancha, donde el equipo es colista de la Euroliga con una victoria en ocho encuentros y la llegada de Velimir Perasovic al club por cuarta vez aún no le ha hecho reaccionar: cinco encuentros entre Liga Endesa y Europa y cinco derrotas. Pero es más grave lo que sucede en las gradas, donde, en una situación insólita, los aficionados abuchearon a la directiva durante la derrota del Real Madrid este martes (86-104). Que sólo acudieran 8.136 personas al Buesa Arena ya podía interpretarse como un castigo. "Sin rumbo ni planificación deportiva, el Araba se vacía", podía leerse en una pancarta que mostraron durante el primer cuarto los miembros Indar Baskonia, el grupo de aficionados más reconocido. Fue la mejor afluencia de espectadores en lo que va de temporada, pero el coliseo vitoriano registró una preocupante media entrada cuando la llegada del Madrid despierta siempre gran expectación y es considerado uno de los partidos del curso. Es la primera vez en años que no se llega a los 10.000 espectadores con el conjunto blanco como rival en la Euroliga. Y no sólo eso, muchos de los que sí acudieron lo hicieron para expresar su malestar con el presidente Josean Querejeta, hasta ahora intocable, en forma de silbidos y pañolada por las últimas decisiones tomadas por el club. Como respuesta al malestar de los aficionados, Joseba, el hijo del presidente, dejó un mensaje en sus redes sociales. "Cuatro Ligas, siete Copas del Rey, cinco Supercopas, una Copa Korac y seis Final Four. Todo esto en una ciudad de 250.000 habitantes. Que venga el siguiente y lo iguale", escribió. En el epicentro de todo, Paolo Galbiati, al que el Baskonia destituyó el pasado 14 de octubre. Nunca un entrenador del club había durado tan poco al inicio de una temporada. Eso es mucho decir comprobando la ristra de inquilinos del banquillo en los últimos tiempos: nada menos que 13, con varias etapas de algunos, desde 2009. El club argumentó que el técnico tenía "un mensaje derrotista y lleno de excusas". Lo cierto es que su plantilla estaba incompleta y la actual aún lo está después de una horrible planificación. Que había lidiado con lesiones y también lo está haciendo Perasovic. Y que apenas había podido trabajar, como le sucede al croata. "Es hasta imposible poder entrenar así", lamentó el nuevo técnico en un discurso semejante al de su antecesor aludiendo a las bajas tras perder este domingo frente al Valencia Basket. Los vitorianos disputaron el choque frente al Madrid con sólo nueve jugadores del primer equipo y sin Tadas Sedekerskis, Rodions Kurucs y Chris Duarte. El crecimiento de la perla Stefan Joksimovic es el único motivo de alegría... y todo apunta a que volará en verano. El despido de Galbiati estaba cantado desde hacía meses. El Baskonia no le quería, pero sí aspiraba a sacar tajada económica si se marchaba al Barcelona, que le pretendía. Esa operación no se terminó dando y los vitorianos tuvieron que arrancar la temporada con un entrenador en el que no creían. Recurrieron a Perasovic, que va ya por su cuarto advenimiento en Vitoria, pero de momento el equipo no arranca por todos los males anteriores. Además de las protestas hacia el palco, durante el encuentro ante el Madrid hubo cánticos y algunas pancartas a favor de Galbiati. Su salida es una de las principales razones del malestar y de la desafección de la afición baskonista. El técnico italiano no sólo había conectado con la grada y el vestuario, sino que había dado al club su primera Copa del Rey desde 2009. El club le despidió justo antes de afrontar cinco partidos a domicilio, pero en el el regreso del equipo al Buesa Arena los espectadores no se olvidaron de él. Perasovic, viejo ídolo, tuvo un amargo regreso por todo lo vivido y también por la derrota, pero tiene confianza en revertir la situación. "La gente pueda estar decepcionada, pero la situación puede cambiar rápido, aunque la paciencia no existe en el baloncesto", aseguró tras la derrota ante el Madrid. Y mandó un mensaje de optimismo: "Con la vuelta de los lesionados y algún jugador que nos dé un salto de calidad, esto será otra historia". Porque confirmó también que están en el mercado buscando "algo bueno, bonito y barato". En el segundo partido de esta doble jornada de Euroliga, el Baskonia visita este viernes al ASVEL Villeurbanne. Poco menos que una final para no perder ya, a finales de octubre, todas sus aspiraciones en la Euroliga. El fin de semana, se mide al Kids&Us Manresa, colista de la Liga Endesa. Hay temporada por delante para intentar levantarse, pero estas dos citas son fundamentales para tratar de atajar una crisis que va más allá de la cancha.
